content: If you miss a dose of this medication, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage instructions, refer to the product guidelines and consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. Important Note on Usage of This Information: The information provided here is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common Brand Name(s): Primaxin Uses: This medication is used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of antibiotics known as carbapenem-type antibiotics. How to Use: This medication is administered via injection into a muscle or vein as directed by your doctor, typically every 6 to 8 hours. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare provider on preparation and usage. Before using, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed treatment duration, even if symptoms resolve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, this medication may cause upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions: Before using imipenem with cilastatin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to either of its ingredients, other carbapenems (e.g., meropenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is known to pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription/non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine glucose tests), potentially causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Additional Notes: This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney/liver function tests) may be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to determine a new dosing schedule. Storage: Follow the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for proper storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024.
